name: Proper Stable Sample Compression / Proper Equivalence Queries Complexity (affine)
details: There are no constants $c>0,d$ such that $\mathrm{psUSC}(\mathcal H)\geq c\,\mathrm Q_{\mathrm{peq}}(\mathcal H)-d$ for every finite binary class.
proof: For the half-interval family $\mathcal I_n$, proper stable unlabeled compression has value one, while proper equivalence-query complexity is $\Theta(\log n)$. Hence the asserted reverse affine-linear bound fails.
witness_verification: The recorded values are $\mathrm{psUSC}(\mathcal I_n)=1$ and $\mathrm Q_{\mathrm{peq}}(\mathcal I_n)=\Theta(\log n)$, so the gap is unbounded.
